in_context.text: The elder warns that deceivers are going about who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. He tells the readers not to take such a teacher into their house or send him on with a greeting. This verse gives the reason: whoever welcomes him shares in his evil work.

speaker.text: "The elder," who does not give his name. Early Christian tradition identifies him as John the apostle.

audience.text: "The elect lady and her children." This may be a Christian woman and her family, or a figurative name for a local church. The letter does not say which.

affected.text: Travelling teachers who do not bring the doctrine of Christ, and anyone who welcomes and supports them.

what.text: Welcoming a false teacher is not neutral. The one who sends him on his way with a greeting takes a share in what he is doing. Other Scripture also warns against being a "partaker of other men's sins."

events.text: Christian teachers travelled between churches and relied on believers to house them. Some taught that Jesus Christ had not come in the flesh.

written.text: Traditional: about AD 85-95, late in John's life. Scholarly: most also place it in the late first century, though some think "the elder" was a church leader other than the apostle.

where.text: The letter does not say where it was written or sent. Early tradition places John's last years in Ephesus, and the readers were likely in the province of Asia.

purpose.text: The elder wants the readers to protect what they have worked for and not lose their full reward. Housing and sending off false teachers would help spread their teaching.

big_picture.text: The letter holds truth and love together. Love means walking in God's commandments, and hospitality must not become support for teaching that denies Christ came in the flesh.

for_readers.text: Readers are reminded that helping someone's work makes you part of it. Scripture repeatedly calls God's people not to share in others' sins.

misuse.popular_reading: Quoted as a rule to refuse any kindness, conversation, or greeting to anyone who holds different beliefs on any matter.

in_context_reading.text: The warning is about deceivers who deny that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh and who do not abide in the doctrine of Christ. The concern is taking such teachers into the house and sending them on, which would support their work.

why_it_matters.text: The word means "to rejoice, be glad," and in this infinitive form it was used as a common greeting. The elder is speaking of the greeting given to the visiting teacher.
It means to have a share of, go shares in, take part in. The same verb appears in 1 Timothy 5:22, "neither be partaker of other men's sins."
In an ethical sense it means bad, evil, wicked. It describes the deceiver's works, the teaching that denies Christ came in the flesh.

takeaway.text: Love does not mean helping spread a denial of Christ. Whoever welcomes and sends on such a teacher shares in his work.
